conviction_note: The event is confirmed by the company. Every material item since the July print is a public company release: the Q3 dividend already declared at $0.75 through November, the 6%-to-8% note refinancing, the CFO leaving for health reasons, and hedged dividend wording. At 0.72x the last NAV and a 18% yield the stock already prices a dividend cut, and the bar is unresolved ($0.49 vs $0.55), so I have no unpriced finding and emit an honest 0.

outside_window.finding: The 2026-09-09 dividend release changed its wording. June said 'pleased to continue delivering strong current income'; September says 'in this challenging macro environment while carefully considering current and expected earnings levels, portfolio dynamics and our spillover position'. With adjusted NII covering 63% of the dividend, that points to a reset at the next declaration, around 2026-12-09 on the June/September cadence. The Q3 $0.75 is already declared through November, so no cut can land in this release. The stock's 18% yield already prices a cut.

searched_and_found_nothing: Event check: the company announced the Oct 6 amc release with a call on Oct 7 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/17/3363967/0/en/saratoga-investment-corp-to-report-fiscal-second-quarter-2027-financial-results-and-hold-conference-call.html). Confirmed.
Ex-dividend: the September $0.25 has record date 2026-10-06, so under T+1 it goes ex on Oct 6, before the entry close. It is not inside the trade window.

424B2 prospectus supplement of 2026-09-24 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1377936/000121390026102998/ea0306350-424b2_saratoga.htm): its Recent Developments section has no preliminary 8/31 NAV or NII estimate. It shows the 6.00% 2027 notes ($105.5M) redeemed on 2026-09-18, and $196M of 2027-dated notes still outstanding (including 4.35% $75M). There is no capitalization table later than 5/31.

Financing (lesson 4 question): $97.75M of 8.00% 2031 notes (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/18/3347332/0/en/saratoga-investment-corp-prices-public-offering-of-85-0-million-8-00-notes-due-2031.html) refinance the 6% 2027s, and $20.08M pays down the floating Valley SPV line (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/23/3367835/0/en/saratoga-investment-corp-prices-public-offering-of-additional-20-08-million-8-00-notes-due-2031.html). This is terming out maturities, not funding distress. The extra cost is about +$0.02-0.03/share/quarter from Q3. The Fed's 25bp hike on 2026-09-16 (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html) adds about +$0.03/quarter on a floating asset book funded mostly at fixed rates. The two roughly cancel, and both are public. Net 0.

CFO Henri Steenkamp stepping down effective 10/31 for health reasons; the controller becomes principal financial officer. No disagreement is disclosed, he stays on the board and as SBIC CFO, and no NT filing was made (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/18/3364940/0/en/saratoga-investment-corp-announces-cfo-transition-and-new-leadership-appointments.html). 0.

Form 4 activity: only a 2,560-share indirect transfer by the CEO on 2026-07-22 as employee compensation (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/SAR/form-4-saratoga-investment-corp-insider-trading-activity-a42dc44fe1f0.html). There is no open-market buying into the drawdown, and no buybacks in Q1 per the 8-K exhibit.
2026 proxy: no proposal to sell shares below NAV, so no dilution overhang (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/SAJ/def-14a-saratoga-investment-corp-definitive-proxy-statement-c42fb566f95b.html).

Exigo (red watchlist, $17.3M at 70% of cost, still accruing in Q1): I found no restructuring or bankruptcy news. A move to non-accrual would cost about $0.04/share/quarter, but I have no document saying it happened.
August 2026 leveraged loan index data, for the 8/31 marks: not retrievable. Calendar Q2 loans returned +1.93%. Using this would be a macro-to-company inference anyway.

baseline_tension: Nothing I found cuts against the tape. The stock is at its 52-week low, at a 28% discount to NAV and an 18% yield, and has fallen on 6 of its last 7 prints. The expected dividend cut, the NII shortfall and the falling NAV are already in the price, so the price has all of this.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: the only draft finding was the hedged dividend wording. The decision it points to is the December declaration, outside the exit window, and Q3 is already declared, so I moved it from findings to outside_window. The pre-lessons sum of -0.5 becomes 0.
Lesson 3: that draft finding's own why_not_priced said an 18% yield already prices a cut, so it argued itself away. That is a second reason to drop it rather than size it.
Lesson 6 (bar): consensus is $0.49 vs $0.55 with no company guide, so the bar is unsourced and any size would have been capped. With no findings left this does not change a number.
Lesson 4: I asked what the note issuance buys (refinancing 2027 maturities, not distress) and signed it 0 rather than negative.
Lesson 5 and the pessimism note: the six-of-seven negative reaction history and the September underperformance are base rates and an unexplained drawdown, not findings, so they stay at 0.
